relationship: Changing incidence angle and the refractive-index boundary connects refraction to the critical threshold and total internal reflection, with calculation checked against the visible ray behaviour.

learnerLoop.action: Rotate the source, observe both regimes, mark the limiting ray, calculate a new threshold, then reverse the media.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Snell’s law and unpolarised Fresnel reflectance derive from the same two refractive indices and incidence angle.
learnerLoop.evidence: An escaping ray becomes a grazing ray and then disappears; normal-referenced angles and calculation agree.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Calculate another threshold or test whether any threshold exists for a reversed pair.

invariants: Angles are measured from the normal and refraction follows the same index ratio used in the calculation.
A critical angle exists only from higher to lower refractive index; total internal reflection requires exceeding it.
Guidance levels change calculation support without removing the physical threshold investigation.
safeAdaptations: Change index examples and prediction wording within the existing optical model.
Adjust working support while preserving the observe, mark and calculate sequence.
nonGoals: Do not present total internal reflection as occurring at every boundary or every angle.
Do not expand into wave interference or a full optical-instrument simulator.

prompt.description: One current model task and one short action prompt.

model.description: Snell’s law and unpolarised Fresnel reflectance derive from the same two refractive indices and incidence angle.
model.visibility: Always visible; later controls are progressively disclosed.

working.description: Consistent worked examples linked to the model precede required learner calculations; the same rows, quantities and units carry through.

evidence.description: An escaping ray becomes a grazing ray and then disappears; normal-referenced angles and calculation agree.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: Advances only after the current model-derived criterion.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

angle.description: Angle of incidence measured from the normal.
angle.domain: 5 to 80 degrees; first step limited to 35 degrees.
angle.output: Rays, reflected/transmitted power, angular marks and regime.

critical.description: c = asin(n outside / n inside), only if n inside > n outside.
critical.domain: Degrees; no critical angle when the index condition fails.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Final open mode keeps all variables within the original conceptual model, comparison readings and reset.

dependencies: Rotate beyond 29 degrees, while limited below the first critical angle.
Observe angles on both sides of c and mark within 0.55 degrees; the accepted marker snaps to c.
Replace glass with diamond, then supply the index ratio and inverse-sine result and test the beam. Earlier working shows the same calculation for glass. Edits immediately clear success.
Observe the reversed boundary near both ends of the angle range.
Ungated experiment: change either medium, mark/inspect thresholds, and keep measured readings.
implementation.completion: Every guided criterion is evaluated from actual model state. Continue never bypasses an unmet criterion. Restart returns to the first step; Back repeats a prior step.
limitations: Ideal lossless flat boundary; radial entry through the semicircular face is normal to that face. Unpolarised Fresnel power. The grazing ray at c indicates a limiting direction.
Ray lengths are illustrative. A minimum ray opacity preserves visibility; the saved power values are physical model values.
